mandatoryCriteria: ATT-01: Authorized editor requests bounded upload and sees progress/cancel; private staging cannot attach files across projects.
ATT-02: Accept validated PNG/JPEG/WebP bytes with size/dimension/count caps; reject SVG/HTML/spoofed MIME and finalize only after verification.
ATT-03: Finalized images show filename/size/thumbnail and preview; failed or pending upload is not shown as a saved attachment.
ATT-04: Authenticated proxy checks current project access on every fetch; no public bucket/long-lived URL or project-revocation bypass.
ATT-05: Uploader or owner/manager removes image with confirmation/history; removed images are absent from active card and cleanup is retryable.
ATT-06: Expired uploads/unreferenced objects are cleaned safely; quotas fail visibly without breaking existing saved card fields.
ATT-07: Trashing card preserves finalized files until restore cutoff; restore recovers them and purge never destroys a successfully restored card's images.
DEL-01: Owner/manager confirms Delete, moves card to trash with server deletedAt/restoreUntil and immediately excludes it from active counts/search.
DEL-02: Owner/manager lists trashed cards with actor/deadline and restore action; member/viewer cannot browse trash.
DEL-03: Owner/manager restores same ID/content/comments/finalized images strictly before server cutoff; no-op repeats do not extend deadline.
DEL-04: Original valid column/nearest surviving position is default; absent/read-only destination requires explicit authorized active target or reopening board.
DEL-05: At or after deletedAt plus exactly 24 hours restore returns stable expired response even if cleanup has not run.
DEL-06: Conditional state/version and job fencing allow one winner; cleanup cannot purge restored data or files.
DEL-07: After cutoff remove recoverable content/files via retryable cleanup; retain minimal audit/duplicate tombstones with no deleted body.
DEL-08: Trashed/expired cards reject edits/moves/comments/new uploads; UI explains disappearance while retaining safe unsent drafts.

Mounted operations enforce current identity, role/target authority, project and board grants, resource ancestry, lifecycle and receipt replay boundaries; negative cases cannot expose data or write effects.
Applicable writes preserve state/version, minimal receipt, activity and outbox atomically; real separate-connection tests cover the feature races and retention limits.

Every listed backend feature requires a fresh independent review of its complete reachable frozen source, fixed weights/category minima, unrounded score strictly greater than8.5, no blocker and actual passing checks. Builders cannot approve their own work.

Required UI and integration phases need actual test/browser evidence with current backend/UI hash bindings; source or API tests alone cannot prove UI or real-provider/hosted acceptance. Do not relabel missing mandatory behavior deferred to close a feature.
scopeAndExclusions: Current listed product features and reachable shared dependencies; PostgreSQL Node/Worker and Next static UI. Review alone does not approve unexecuted UI/hosted/provider/deployment behavior. Real OAuth must not be replaced with an email-only session. Direct UAT after all local gates pass; hosted checks remain UAT pending until run. No dev/production. Reconciled retirements preserve stableIDs and precede scoring. No real credentials or live-user data in tests/logs.
releaseSequenceClarification: User explicitly clarified2026-11-03: all local gates pass and source freezes, deploy UAT directly, then finish hosted checks. Host-dependent checks remain UAT pending and are not falsely closed. No dev or production.

requiredTestsExpansion.reason: Before final review/source freeze, explicitly require existing generated-contract parity, embedded-SQL parity and actual local browser/MCP integration commands. This adds checks without changing or weakening any acceptance statement or score threshold.
requiredTestsExpansion.runnerEnvironment: Runner must supply explicit disposable loopback PostgreSQL test URLs, NODE_ENV=test and the documented local browser executable/runtime; commands do not use production or hosted user data.
